newsitem.title: New Zealand: RUGBY LEAGUE-NZ COMPLETE SERIES WHITEWASH AGAINST BRITAIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-NZ COMPLETE SERIES WHITEWASH AGAINST BRITAIN.

text.p: New Zealand completed only their second 3-0 rugby league test series whitewash in 89 years over Britain when they crushed the Lions 32-12 in the third test at Lancaster Park on Friday.

The 20-point difference beat New Zealand's previous highest winning margin of 19 points, set twice in the 1962 series, and also equalled their previous highest score against Britain set in 1984 when they made their first series clean sweep.
Coach Phil Larder took responsibility for Britain's disastrous New Zealand tour in which they failed to win one match in six outings.
"If anybody has to be criticised, it should be me," he said. "The players put their bodies on the line, they gave 100 percent commitment.
"The odds were stacked against us but every one of them can hold their heads up."
Matthew Ridge's New Zealand side went into the final test having beaten Britain 17-12 and 18-15 in the first two tests.
In an absorbing first half New Zealand were relentless as they threw the ball around in dizzying fashion against a tentative British side.

The Lions drew first blood when Denis Betts dived over to score and scrum-half Bobbie Goulding, who did not train with the side all week because of an ankle injury, converted to give Britain a 6-0 lead.
But their joy was shortlived. New Zealand centre John Timu stormed over the line to score four minutes later and Ridge's conversion tied the game at 6-6.
New Zealand, raising the tempo, attacked time and again, forcing Britain to spend much of the rest of the half deep inside their own territory.

With half-back Stacey Jones in superb touch calling the shots, the Kiwis finally broke through again 10 minutes from the break. Jones flicked a short pass to Stephen Kearney who offloaded for centre Ruben Wiki to power over.
Britain suffered a double blow in the last five minutes of the half when Kiwi stand-off Gene Ngamu grabbed an intercept and darted 55 metres to score.
Winger Sean Hoppe added another minutes later to take New Zealand to a 20-6 halftime lead.
The teams exchanged converted tries before Ridge ensured New Zealand's series whitewash when he stepped his way through to score his side's sixth try, which he converted for the 32-12 result.
